slides.title: In providing anticipatory guidance to parents whose child will soon be entering
text: Question: In providing anticipatory guidance to parents whose child will soon be entering kindergarten, which is a critical factor to include in this teaching?
A. The child needs to be able to sit still.
B. The child should attend a preschool program first.
C. The child should be able to count to 25.
D. The parent should have interaction and be responsive to the child.
Correct answer: D. The parent should have interaction and be responsive to the child.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The parent should have interaction and be responsive to the child.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The parent should have interaction and be responsive to the child.” – Responsive interaction supports development
Not correct:
• “The child needs to be able to sit still.” – Not sufficient alone
• “The child should attend a preschool program first.” – Preschool attendance not mandatory
• “The child should be able to count to 25.” – Counting is not the sole readiness indicator
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: The parents of a newborn infant state, “We will probably not have our baby immun
text: Question: The parents of a newborn infant state, “We will probably not have our baby immunized because we are concerned about the risks.” What is the nurse’s best response?
A. “You should probably think about this decision.”
B. “This has to be reported to the health department.”
C. “It is your decision to immunize your child or not.”
D. “It is far riskier to not immunize your baby.”
Correct answer: D. “It is far riskier to not immunize your baby.”
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• “It is far riskier to not immunize your baby.”
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• ““It is far riskier to not immunize your baby.”” – Explains risk; use respectful shared decision-making
Not correct:
• ““You should probably think about this decision.”” – Vague; does not explain risk
• ““This has to be reported to the health department.”” – Reporting not automatically required
• ““It is your decision to immunize your child or not.”” – Respects autonomy but lacks risk education
Not covered in your class PowerPoints, so this answer comes from the quiz file only.

slides.title: A student nurse asks the faculty why peer relationships become more important du
text: Question: A student nurse asks the faculty why peer relationships become more important during adolescence. Which of the following is the nurse’s best response?
A. Adolescents dislike their parents.
B. They provide adolescents with a feeling of belonging.
C. They promote a sense of individuality in adolescents.
D. Adolescents no longer need parental control.
Correct answer: B. They provide adolescents with a feeling of belonging.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• They provide adolescents with a feeling of belonging.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “They provide adolescents with a feeling of belonging.” – Peer groups support belonging
Not correct:
• “Adolescents dislike their parents.” – Not an inherent adolescent trait
• “They promote a sense of individuality in adolescents.” – Peers often reinforce group norms
• “Adolescents no longer need parental control.” – Parental guidance remains important

slides.title: A student nurse is preparing to administer an Hib vaccination to an infant. What
text: Question: A student nurse is preparing to administer an Hib vaccination to an infant. What action by the student requires the registered nurse to intervene?
A. Assesses the family’s beliefs and values about vaccinations
B. Wipes the dorsal gluteal area with alcohol prior to injection
C. Gives the vaccine information statement prior to administering the vaccine
D. Obtains written informed consent before giving the vaccine
Correct answer: B. Wipes the dorsal gluteal area with alcohol prior to injection
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Wipes the dorsal gluteal area with alcohol prior to injection
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Wipes the dorsal gluteal area with alcohol prior to injection” – Dorsogluteal site is inappropriate for routine vaccination
Not correct:
• “Assesses the family’s beliefs and values about vaccinations” – Supports individualized counseling
• “Gives the vaccine information statement prior to administering the vaccine” – VIS should precede vaccine
• “Obtains written informed consent before giving the vaccine” – Consent requirements depend on policy and law

slides.title: The nurse is admitting a patient into the maternity clinic. Which of the followi
text: Question: The nurse is admitting a patient into the maternity clinic. Which of the following would the nurse document as a probable sign of pregnancy?
A. The patient has a positive pregnancy test.
B. The nurse obtains fetal heart rate with a doppler.
C. The patient complains of increased hunger, anxiety, and shakiness.
D. The patient states she has missed her last two menstrual periods.
Correct answer: A. The patient has a positive pregnancy test.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• The patient has a positive pregnancy test.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “The patient has a positive pregnancy test.” – Probable sign, not definitive
Not correct:
• “The nurse obtains fetal heart rate with a doppler.” – Positive sign of pregnancy
• “The patient complains of increased hunger, anxiety, and shakiness.” – Nonspecific symptoms
• “The patient states she has missed her last two menstrual periods.” – Presumptive sign
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 2: “Pregnancy test +”
Your slide also lists a missed period (amenorrhea) as presumptive and the fetal heartbeat as a positive sign, which rules out the other options.

slides.title: The nurse is teaching a pregnant client about the physiological effects and horm
text: Question: The nurse is teaching a pregnant client about the physiological effects and hormonal changes that occur during pregnancy. The client asks the nurse about the purpose of estrogen. The nurse bases the response on which of the following purposes of estrogen?
A. It prevents the involution of the corpus luteum and maintains the production of progesterone until the placenta is formed.
B. It stimulates metabolism of glucose and converts the glucose to fat.
C. It stimulates uterine development to provide an environment for the fetus and stimulates the breasts to prepare for lactation.
D. It maintains the uterine lining for implantation.
Correct answer: C. It stimulates uterine development to provide an environment for the fetus and stimulates the breasts to prepare for lactation.
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• It stimulates uterine development to provide an environment for the fetus and stimulates the breasts to prepare for lactation.
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “It stimulates uterine development to provide an environment for the fetus and stimulate…” – Estrogen supports uterine and breast growth
Not correct:
• “It prevents the involution of the corpus luteum and maintains the production of progest…” – Describes hCG
• “It stimulates metabolism of glucose and converts the glucose to fat.” – Not primary estrogen role
• “It maintains the uterine lining for implantation.” – Describes progesterone

slides.title: The nurse has assisted in performing a nonstress test on a pregnant client and i
text: Question: The nurse has assisted in performing a nonstress test on a pregnant client and is reviewing the documentation related to the results of the test. The nurse notes that the physician has documented the test results as reactive. The nurse interprets that this result indicates (select an answer from the following options):
A. That the findings on the monitor were difficult to interpret
B. Abnormal findings
C. Normal findings
D. The need for further evaluation
Correct answer: C. Normal findings
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Normal findings
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Normal findings” – Reactive NST indicates reassuring accelerations
Not correct:
• “That the findings on the monitor were difficult to interpret” – Reactive is an interpretable reassuring result
• “Abnormal findings” – Reactive is generally reassuring
• “The need for further evaluation” – Reactive result alone does not require additional evaluation

slides.title: The nurse is assisting in caring for a client in the active stage of labor. The
text: Question: The nurse is assisting in caring for a client in the active stage of labor. The nurse is told that the fetal patterns show a late deceleration on the monitor strip. Based on this finding, the nurse prepares for which most appropriate nursing actions?
A. Documenting the findings and continuing to monitor the fetal patterns
B. Increasing the rate of the intravenous (IV) oxytocin infusion
C. Administering oxygen via face mask
D. Placing the mother in a supine position
Correct answer: C. Administering oxygen via face mask
Topic: Maternal-Newborn
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Administering oxygen via face mask
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Administering oxygen via face mask” – Source choice; oxygen is not routine if mother is normoxic
Not correct:
• “Documenting the findings and continuing to monitor the fetal patterns” – Does not address nonreassuring pattern
• “Increasing the rate of the intravenous (IV) oxytocin infusion” – May worsen uterine tachysystole or fetal compromise
• “Placing the mother in a supine position” – May worsen vena cava compression
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 78: “Provide O2 to mother”
• Unit 5 - OB and Newborn Care, slide 78: “Position mother on left side”

slides.title: Which defect results in increased pulmonary blood flow?
text: Question: Which defect results in increased pulmonary blood flow?
A. Tricuspid atresia
B. Transposition of the great arteries
C. Atrial septal defect
D. Pulmonic stenosis
Correct answer: C. Atrial septal defect
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Atrial septal defect
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Atrial septal defect” – Left-to-right shunt increases pulmonary flow
Not correct:
• “Tricuspid atresia” – Cyanotic lesion restricts pulmonary flow
• “Transposition of the great arteries” – Parallel circulations cause cyanosis
• “Pulmonic stenosis” – Obstructs pulmonary flow
✔ Checked against your PowerPoints:
• Unit 5 - Pediatrics, slide 27: “Atrial and Ventricular septal defect”

slides.title: For what reason might a newborn infant with a cardiac defect, such as coarctatio
text: Question: For what reason might a newborn infant with a cardiac defect, such as coarctation of the aorta, that results in a right-to-left shunt receive prostaglandin E1?
A. To decrease inflammation
B. To improve oxygenation
C. To control pain
D. To decrease respirations
Correct answer: B. To improve oxygenation
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• To improve oxygenation
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “To improve oxygenation” – Increases available oxygen
Not correct:
• “To decrease inflammation” – Oxygen does not directly reduce inflammation
• “To control pain” – Not an analgesic
• “To decrease respirations” – Not intended to suppress breathing

slides.title: A parent asks the nurse why self-monitoring of blood glucose is being recommende
text: Question: A parent asks the nurse why self-monitoring of blood glucose is being recommended for her child with diabetes. The nurse should base the explanation on the knowledge that
A. children are better able to manage the diabetes.
B. it is not as accurate as laboratory testing.
C. the parents are better able to manage the disease.
D. it is a less expensive method of testing.
Correct answer: A. children are better able to manage the diabetes.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• children are better able to manage the diabetes.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “children are better able to manage the diabetes.” – Supports age-appropriate self-management
Not correct:
• “it is not as accurate as laboratory testing.” – Home monitoring is useful despite measurement limits
• “the parents are better able to manage the disease.” – Parent support helps but child autonomy is focus
• “it is a less expensive method of testing.” – Cost is not primary advantage

text: Question: The nurse is reviewing the physician’s documentation in the record of a child admitted with a diagnosis of intussusception. The nurse expects to note that the physician has documented the presence of:
A. Currant jelly–type stools
B. Scleral jaundice
C. Pale-colored and hard stools
D. Projectile vomiting
Correct answer: A. Currant jelly–type stools
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Currant jelly–type stools
(This answer was inferred when the master guide was put together; it is not keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Currant jelly–type stools” – Blood and mucus suggest intussusception
Not correct:
• “Scleral jaundice” – Suggests bilirubin accumulation
• “Pale-colored and hard stools” – Not classic intussusception stool
• “Projectile vomiting” – More typical of pyloric stenosis

slides.title: Therapeutic management of most children with Hirschsprung disease is primarily
text: Question: Therapeutic management of most children with Hirschsprung disease is primarily
A. permanent colostomy.
B. low-fiber diet.
C. surgical removal of the affected section of the bowel.
D. daily enemas.
Correct answer: C. surgical removal of the affected section of the bowel.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• surgical removal of the affected section of the bowel.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “surgical removal of the affected section of the bowel.” – Removes nonfunctioning aganglionic segment
Not correct:
• “permanent colostomy.” – Usually not permanently required
• “low-fiber diet.” – Does not correct aganglionosis
• “daily enemas.” – Does not definitively treat condition

slides.title: What is the major concern guiding treatment for the child with Legg-Calvé-Perthe
text: Question: What is the major concern guiding treatment for the child with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease?
A. Encourage new hobbies.
B. Minimize pain.
C. Maintain normal activities.
D. Avoid permanent deformity.
Correct answer: D. Avoid permanent deformity.
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Avoid permanent deformity.
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Avoid permanent deformity.” – Preserve joint function and prevent deformity
Not correct:
• “Encourage new hobbies.” – May support coping but not primary outcome
• “Minimize pain.” – Important but not long-term deformity prevention
• “Maintain normal activities.” – Supports development but not the primary orthopedic goal

slides.title: A 6-year-old patient who has been placed in skeletal traction has pain, edema, a
text: Question: A 6-year-old patient who has been placed in skeletal traction has pain, edema, and fever. The nurse should assess which of the following?
A. Warmth at site of pain
B. Blood pressure
C. Range of motion of all extremities
D. Neurologic status
Correct answer: A. Warmth at site of pain
Topic: Pediatrics
notes: Rationale:
Weekly quiz key (one answer):
• Warmth at site of pain
(This answer is keyed in the original quiz source.)
Study notes from your master guide (not official Galen rationales):
• “Warmth at site of pain” – Pain, edema and fever plus localized warmth may suggest pin-site infection
Not correct:
• “Blood pressure” – Systemic measure less specific to local infection
• “Range of motion of all extremities” – Moving a tractioned limb may be inappropriate; does not identify infection
• “Neurologic status” – Less specific for suspected pin-site infection
